directAnswer: Pope Francis was Jorge Mario Bergoglio, a Jesuit and archbishop of Buenos Aires who reigned from 13 March 2013 until his death on 21 April 2025. The first pope from the Americas, the first Jesuit pope and the first to take the name Francis, he emphasized mercy and care for the poor, wrote Laudato si' on care for creation, and led a multi-year Synod on synodality.

sections.h2: Jorge Mario Bergoglio of Buenos Aires
paras: Jorge Mario Bergoglio was born on 17 December 1936 in Buenos Aires, Argentina, the son of Italian immigrants. He trained as a chemical technician before entering the Society of Jesus in 1958, and was ordained a priest in 1969. He served as Jesuit provincial of Argentina from 1973 to 1979, during the years of military dictatorship, and later as rector of a Jesuit seminary.

John Paul II named him auxiliary bishop of Buenos Aires in 1992, archbishop in 1998, and cardinal in 2001. As archbishop he was known for living in a simple apartment, using public transportation, and frequently visiting the city's poorest neighborhoods.

Elected on 13 March 2013 after the resignation of Benedict XVI, he became the first pope from the Americas and the Southern Hemisphere, the first Jesuit pope, and the first non-European pope in well over a thousand years. He chose the name Francis after St. Francis of Assisi, as a sign of his concern for the poor, for peace and for creation.
He chose to live in the Casa Santa Marta guesthouse rather than the papal apartments. His motto, Miserando atque eligendo, comes from a homily of St. Bede on the call of St. Matthew.

sections.h2: Evangelii gaudium, Laudato si' and Fratelli tutti
paras: His apostolic exhortation Evangelii gaudium (2013) called the Church to missionary joy and to go out to the peripheries. The encyclical Laudato si' (2015) addressed care for our common home, linking environmental degradation, including climate change, to poverty and to a throwaway culture. Fratelli tutti (2020) reflected on human fraternity and social friendship, and Dilexit nos (2024) returned to devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.

Amoris laetitia (2016), following two synods on the family, addressed marriage and family life, and its guidance on accompanying divorced and remarried Catholics generated considerable discussion. He proclaimed an Extraordinary Jubilee of Mercy in 2015–2016.

Francis reorganized the Roman Curia with the apostolic constitution Praedicate Evangelium (2022) and appointed many cardinals from regions never before represented, giving the College a non-European majority. He convened a Synod on synodality that included lay voting members for the first time. His 2021 motu proprio Traditionis custodes placed new restrictions on the pre-conciliar Mass.

He traveled widely, including to the Arabian Peninsula in 2019, where he signed the Document on Human Fraternity in Abu Dhabi. In September 2015 he visited the United States, canonizing St. Junípero Serra in Washington and becoming the first pope to address a joint meeting of Congress, before attending the World Meeting of Families in Philadelphia.

sections.h2: Final Illness and Death on Easter Monday
paras: After a long hospitalization in early 2025, Francis appeared to bless the crowd on Easter Sunday and died the next morning, 21 April 2025, at 88, during the Jubilee Year he had opened. At his request he was buried in the Basilica of St. Mary Major in Rome rather than St. Peter's.

keyFacts: Born Jorge Mario Bergoglio in Buenos Aires on 17 December 1936
First Jesuit pope and first pope from the Americas
Wrote Evangelii gaudium, Laudato si', Amoris laetitia and Fratelli tutti
First pope to address a joint meeting of the U.S. Congress (2015)
Buried in the Basilica of St. Mary Major, Rome

faqs.question: Why did Pope Francis choose the name Francis?
faqs.answer: He chose it in honor of St. Francis of Assisi, explaining soon after his election that the saint represented poverty, peace and care for creation, themes he wanted to define his pontificate.

faqs.question: What is Laudato si' about?
faqs.answer: Published in 2015, Laudato si' calls for care of our common home, connecting environmental problems such as pollution and climate change with poverty, consumerism and the dignity of every human life.

faqs.question: Where is Pope Francis buried?
faqs.answer: At his own request he was buried in the Basilica of St. Mary Major in Rome, a church he visited before and after nearly every papal journey to pray before the Marian icon Salus Populi Romani.
